articles.title: Bolt Property Classes Explained: 4.6 vs 8.8 vs 10.9 vs 12.9
articles.summary: Read bolt strength markings, compare nominal values, and prepare a specification that covers the complete joint.

sections.title: How to read the marking
paragraphs: For carbon and alloy steel bolts, the first number multiplied by 100 gives nominal tensile strength in MPa. The second number divided by 10 gives the nominal yield-to-tensile ratio. Class 8.8 therefore represents 800 MPa nominal tensile strength and a nominal ratio of 0.8.
These numbers explain the designation; they are not a complete acceptance specification. Required minimum properties and test methods depend on the applicable standard, diameter and product geometry.

sections.title: Compare nominal values
paragraphs: Use this table to understand markings, not to calculate a safe working load or an installation torque. MPa is equivalent to N/mm².

sections.title: Choose for the complete joint
paragraphs: A higher class is not automatically a better replacement. Check the specified preload, mating nut, washer, thread engagement, coating and service environment together. Changing the lubricant or finish can change the torque needed to achieve the intended clamp force.
Low and countersunk heads may have reduced loadability. For a countersunk socket screw, check its product standard as well as its property class before applying data from a conventional hex bolt.

sections.title: What to include in your RFQ
paragraphs: State the product standard, thread diameter and pitch, length, property class, finish and quantity. Include the drawing revision and required inspection documents. If replacing an existing fastener, provide its markings and assembly requirements rather than relying on a photograph alone.

articles.title: Understanding GB/T 32076.7: High Strength Bolt Assemblies for Steel Structures
articles.summary: A purchasing guide to the M39–M64 scope, assembly requirements and documentation for GB/T 32076.7.

sections.title: Check the standard scope
paragraphs: GB/T 32076.7-2015 covers M39–M64 large-width-across-flats hexagon bolt and nut assemblies for preloaded structural connections. It is not a general specification for every high strength bolt or every metric diameter.

The official Chinese standard record lists publication on 9 October 2015 and implementation on 1 June 2016. Identify the required edition in the purchase specification and check the project documents before ordering.

sections.title: Specify the assembly
paragraphs: Describe the bolt and nut combination, and identify any washers required by the project. State the diameter, pitch, length, property class, finish and required quantities for each component. A bolt that looks similar is not evidence that the complete assembly meets the same requirements.
Keep delivery identification and inspection records with the supplied lots. When reviewing alternatives, compare dimensional and assembly requirements before agreeing to substitute another standard.

sections.title: Agree the installation requirements
paragraphs: A strength class alone does not establish an installation torque. Ask the project engineer to identify the required preload, tightening method and acceptance checks. Confirm that any supplied lubrication and coating match the agreed installation procedure.
Do not assume that a torque value used on a smaller bolt, another coating or a different assembly can be scaled directly to an M39–M64 connection.

sections.title: Before issuing a purchase order
paragraphs: Attach the approved drawing and standard edition. Ask the supplier to confirm dimensional compliance, assembly identification, required mechanical tests, coating details and traceability documents. Record any proposed deviation explicitly so that the project team can review it before manufacture.

articles.title: Surface Treatment Comparison: Zinc Plating vs HDG vs Zinc Flake
articles.summary: Compare coating processes, thread fit and hydrogen-embrittlement considerations before requesting a fastener quotation.

sections.title: Zinc electroplating
paragraphs: ISO 4042 addresses electroplated coating systems for fasteners, including zinc and zinc alloys. A finish specification should identify the coating system, any conversion layer, sealer and lubricant, rather than only a colour.

The standard includes requirements and recommendations to reduce hydrogen-embrittlement risk. For high strength fasteners, agree the process controls and applicable verification with the supplier before choosing an electroplated finish.

sections.title: Hot-dip galvanizing
paragraphs: ISO 10684 covers spun hot-dip galvanized coatings on coarse-threaded steel fasteners from M8 to M64, up to class 10.9 for bolts, screws and studs and class 12 for nuts. Its scope should not be extended automatically to class 12.9 bolts.
Specify the mating thread arrangement and check fit after coating. The coating and nut thread allowances belong in the assembly specification, not just in a note describing the desired appearance.

sections.title: Zinc flake coatings
paragraphs: ISO 10683 covers non-electrolytically applied zinc flake systems. These systems are used on high strength fasteners to address internal hydrogen-embrittlement concerns associated with coating processes. Preparation and application still need controlled procedures.
Confirm the complete coating system, including topcoat and lubricant. A trade name alone does not define corrosion performance, friction behaviour or suitability for the intended joint.

sections.title: Compare quotations on the same basis
paragraphs: Give each supplier the same service environment, corrosion test and acceptance criteria, thread-fit requirements, friction requirements and quantity. Ask for the process specification and relevant test results. Compare the quoted coating system and inspection scope, not colour or price alone.

articles.title: 42CrMo Alloy Steel: Properties and Applications in Fastener Manufacturing
articles.summary: Specify the material standard, heat-treatment condition and finished-fastener requirements when sourcing chromium-molybdenum steel fasteners.

sections.title: Start with the exact material designation
paragraphs: Write the material grade together with its governing standard and delivery condition. Avoid specifying only “alloy steel” when the drawing requires a particular chemistry or mechanical performance.

42CrMo, 42CrMo4 and SAE 4140 are related designations, but they should not be accepted as automatic substitutes. Compare the governing specifications, chemical limits, product form and required tests before approving a substitution. Ovako lists 4140 among similar designations for 42CrMo4 and identifies specific variants separately.

sections.title: Heat treatment and section size matter
paragraphs: Ovako describes 42CrMo4 as a quenching and tempering steel and reports mechanical properties by delivery condition and bar diameter. This illustrates why a grade name alone does not determine the properties of every finished part.

For a fastener quotation, state the required finished-part property class or mechanical specification. Ask how heat treatment, section size and final testing will be controlled for the supplied product.

sections.title: Read certificates against the order
paragraphs: Check that the certificate identifies the specified grade and material standard, heat or lot number, delivery condition and required test results. Confirm how the material identification is carried through to the finished fastener lot.
A raw-material certificate does not by itself verify the dimensions, coating or final mechanical properties of a finished bolt. Request the inspection records required by the purchase specification.

sections.title: Prepare a useful material enquiry
paragraphs: Send the drawing revision, material standard, finished dimensions, required strength and toughness, service temperature, surface treatment and quantity. If an alternative material is proposed, request a comparison of the requirements and obtain approval before production.

articles.title: SEMS Screws: Washer Configuration and Factory Ordering
articles.summary: Specify the screw and washer combination together, then confirm assembly clearance, material, finish and batch demand.

sections.title: Specify the complete assembly
paragraphs: SEMS ordering starts with the screw head, drive, thread and retained washer configuration. State whether you need a flat washer, a spring washer or a combination. Include washer inside diameter, outside diameter, thickness and order in the assembly.

sections.title: Check the installed envelope
paragraphs: Check the space occupied by the head and washers, tool access and usable thread length against the mating parts. Retaining the washer helps keep components together during handling; it does not by itself establish resistance to loosening in your application.

sections.title: Prepare a batch specification
paragraphs: Send a drawing or approved sample reference, material, finish, batch quantity and delivery schedule. Confirm inspection criteria and packing before production. If washer arrangement or coating changes, review the complete assembly again rather than ordering only by screw diameter.

sources.label: PENCOM — machine screw and SEMS configurations

articles.title: Socket Cap, Button, Low and Countersunk Heads: How to Choose
articles.summary: Compare head clearance, tool access and mounting geometry before specifying a screw for factory assembly.

sections.title: Start with space and tool access
paragraphs: Compare the head diameter and height with the available envelope and tool access. A socket cap head, button head and low head solve different clearance problems. Check the actual product drawing instead of treating all screws with the same thread as interchangeable.

sections.title: Match the head to the seating surface
paragraphs: A countersunk head needs a matching countersink; a flat-bearing head needs its specified seating surface. Confirm the head angle, hole preparation and length convention in the drawing. A flush appearance alone does not establish that the joint is correctly specified.

sections.title: Review loadability before substitution
paragraphs: Some low-head and countersunk designs have reduced loadability because of head geometry. Do not transfer torque or load assumptions from a conventional cap screw without checking the applicable product standard. ISO 10642 explicitly covers countersunk socket screws with reduced loadability.

sources.label: ISO 10642 — countersunk screws with reduced loadability

articles.title: Custom Fastener RFQ Checklist for Factory Bulk Orders
articles.summary: Prepare drawings, acceptance requirements and delivery information so a custom fastener enquiry can be reviewed efficiently.

sections.title: Identify the drawing and critical features
paragraphs: Include the drawing number, revision, units and required quantity. Identify critical head, thread, shoulder and washer dimensions, tolerances and mating parts. State the referenced standard or approved sample. A photo can explain appearance but cannot replace dimensional requirements.

sections.title: Define material, finish and acceptance
paragraphs: State material, property requirements and surface treatment separately. Explain which dimensions or tests require inspection records, and whether sample approval is needed before the production batch. Agree on acceptance criteria and document requirements before manufacture; avoid leaving them until delivery.

sections.title: Plan the production and delivery batches
paragraphs: Separate the first batch quantity from annual demand. Provide the destination, target schedule, packing requirements and any split deliveries. Confirm sample arrangements, order quantity and lead time for the specific project. These details support quotation without assuming a universal minimum order or delivery promise.

sources.label: PENCOM — machine screw and SEMS configurations

articles.title: Stainless Steel Fastener Galling: Assembly and Ordering Guide
articles.summary: Plan thread condition, lubrication and assembly trials before ordering stainless steel fasteners in batches.

sections.title: Understand thread seizure
paragraphs: Galling can occur when mating threads adhere under friction. Stainless steel corrosion resistance does not prevent this assembly problem. A seized thread may damage both components; increasing force is not a reliable remedy.

sections.title: Agree on lubrication and surface condition
paragraphs: Discuss compatible lubrication or surface treatments for the application. Record the agreed condition in the purchasing specification. Validate the tightening procedure with that condition; a lubricant change should not inherit an unreviewed torque setting.

sections.title: Prepare a representative assembly trial
paragraphs: Send the mating part specification, service environment and planned assembly method with the RFQ. Confirm samples, assembly checks and acceptance criteria before releasing a production batch. This guide does not establish a universal tightening torque.

sources.label: Stainless Steel Fastener Galling: Assembly and Ordering Guide — Bossard

articles.title: High-Strength Fastener Coatings: Hydrogen Embrittlement Review
articles.summary: Review coating processes, inspection requirements and application conditions together before placing a bulk order.

sections.title: Look beyond coating appearance
paragraphs: Hydrogen embrittlement can cause delayed failure after assembly. Acid cleaning and electroplating can introduce hydrogen into susceptible fasteners. A clean appearance or completed assembly does not establish that this risk has been controlled.

sections.title: Specify the complete coating process
paragraphs: Provide the fastener material and property requirements alongside the coating specification. Ask for a process review, applicable standards and documented controls. Treat hydrogen relief as a qualified process requirement, rather than an automatic guarantee against failure.

sections.title: Confirm records before batch approval
paragraphs: Agree on process records, required testing and sample approval before manufacture. Keep corrosion protection, thread fit and assembly requirements in the same review. Final process selection depends on the product and application; this article supplies an RFQ checklist, not a blanket coating approval.

sources.label: High-Strength Fastener Coatings: Hydrogen Embrittlement Review — Bossard
